types.note: A durable note/fact in the personal knowledge base. Opens in the home peek modal; no bespoke editor, so it edits generically.
A recorded decision (what was chosen and why).

types.label: value.path
types.note: A file as a fact (ADR-0027): a thin pointer to a source/doc/S3 object — never a copy of the bytes. Keyed `file/<path>`. Small text (docs) stores `content` inline so query `contains` is full-text over it; binary/large objects carry `s3Key`/`url` instead. The public docs corpus (file/docs/*) is upserted by scripts/docs-sync.mjs and shared read-only to all.

schema.path: string — the file's logical path (e.g. docs/machine.md)
schema.content: string? — inline body, small text only
schema.s3Key: string? — S3 access handle for large/binary objects

types.label: value.name
types.note: One mental model of the latticework (ADR-0045): a named, simplified explanation of how something works, held as ONE fact per model (keyed model/<slug>) so the vector index embeds each individually and inferred similarTo edges (ADR-0030/0031/0032) surface the right model as a LENS beside otherwise-unlinked facts — the latticework as live graph structure, not a list inside a reading blob. `source` refs the reading it was extracted from (projects a `from` edge).

schema.name: string — the model's canonical name
schema.gloss: string — one-line explanation of the model
schema.category: string — latticework discipline (general-thinking-tools | physics-chemistry-biology | systems | numeracy | microeconomics | art | …)
schema.source: ref? — the reading this model was extracted from

fields.name: source
fields.description: the reading this model was extracted from

types.note: ADR-0057: the ONE collections family — a fact that names members (value.members: [keys]) or a query (value.query, the view shape). Presentation facets (group/frame/board) say how it shows up; promotions are facet additions, never rewrites. Members resolve via workspace.edges({around, membership:true}): declared members[] ∪ inbound membership edges (memberOf/inDoc/onBoard/inView), declared array order as seq.

schema.label: string? — the collection's display name
schema.members: string[]? — declared member fact keys, in order
schema.facets: object? — { group?, frame?, board? } presentation facets

types.note: ADR-0057: an edge-with-properties placing a fact IN a collection (the same ADR-0016 shape as canvas-placement and lit's doc-order). Keyed _collection/<coll>/<memberKey>; the key rule projects `<memberKey> memberOf collection:<coll>`. seq/fold ride the membership, never the member.
